records.text: For a fourth consecutive day, thousands protested in Albania against the Kushner-linked real-estate project in a biodiverse region.
records.speaker: Anonymous Source #2 (Ep tXoI0TTKVrs)

appearances.snippet: For the fourth day in a row, thousands of protesters took to the streets of the Albanian capital, brandishing national flags and flamingo shaped cardboard cutouts on sticks. ... The bird has become a symbol of intensifying protests against a vast real estate project linked to Donald Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner in a region known for its rich biodiversity.

verification.notes: Contemporaneous reporting documents thousands gathering in Tirana on June 3 for a fourth consecutive day, carrying flamingo symbols and protesting the Kushner-linked project near the ecologically sensitive Vjosa-Narta wetland.

sources.title: Albanian protests over Kushner-linked coastal resort intensify
sources.relevance: Reports thousands in Tirana on June 3 for a fourth consecutive day near the Vjosa-Narta wetland.

sources.relevance: Confirms thousands, daily protests, flamingo symbols, and biodiversity concerns.

appearances.snippet: The project that has been presented and the scale of the area involved makes it highly destructive. There'll be 10,000 rooms and construction will last 10 to 15 years.

records.text: Affinity Partners' multi-billion-euro project aims to build two ultra-luxury resorts, one in the Narta Lagoon wildlife reserve and one on a former secret military island; new beach barbed wire sparked local outrage.
records.speaker: Anonymous Source #2 (Ep tXoI0TTKVrs)

appearances.snippet: The multi-billion euro project spearheaded by Kushner's investment firm Affinity Partners aims to build two ultra luxury resort complexes, one in the wildlife reserve of the Nata Lagoon area and the other on a remote island that served as a secret military base during the communist regime. On site construction has barely begun but the installation of barbed wire on this beach last week sparked outrage among local residents.

verification.notes: AP confirms two project components: a coastal development in the Narta Lagoon wildlife reserve and a smaller resort on Sazan, a former communist military base. ANSA confirms barbed-wire-topped fencing at the proposed Zvernec site blocked beach access and triggered protests; reporting describes the investment as multi-billion-euro scale.

sources.relevance: Confirms the Narta Lagoon wildlife-reserve component and Sazan former military-base resort component.

records.text: The Albania development investment will not stop while Edi Rama remains in office, though he is open to discussing concerns.
records.speaker: Edi Rama

appearances.snippet: There is no chance that this investment will stop as long as I am here, and in the meantime I am absolutely open, as I have been on other occasions, to discussing it with anyone who has concerns.

verification.notes: A contemporaneous Albanian report quotes Prime Minister Edi Rama saying there was no chance the investment would stop while he remained in office and that he remained open to discussions with critics.

sources.title: Rama Defends Zvernec Investment Project
sources.relevance: Publishes Ramas statement that the investment would not stop while he remained and that he was open to discussion.

verification.notes: ANSA reports that SPAK, Albanias special anti-corruption prosecution office, confirmed opening an investigation into 2024 protected-area and land-ownership changes that enabled the development.
